question.text:
You are evaluating the financial performance of two retail chains based on their profitability ratios: Chain A: Return on Assets (ROA) = 10%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 15% Chain B: Return on Assets (ROA) = 12%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 18%
Which chain has a higher return on assets (ROA)?

answer.text: Both chains have the same ROA
Cannot determine from the given data

explanation.text: The Logic: ROA is read directly off the data: Chain B = 12%, Chain A = 10%. Chain B earns more per rupee of total assets. The Trap: Picking Chain A reverses the numbers; 'same ROA' ignores a 2-percentage-point gap; 'cannot determine' is wrong because both ROAs are explicitly given. Cross-Exam Context: ROA questions appear in NISM XV, X-A and V-A (for analysing debt-issuer profitability). Distributor's Pro-Tip: For asset-heavy sectors (retail, manufacturing, airlines) ROA beats ROE as the screening metric — it is not inflated by leverage, which is exactly the story retail chains love to sell.
